access.waitMinutes: Try again in about {count} minutes. The button counts down the time.
access.waitUnderMinute: Try again in less than a minute. The button counts down the time.
access.login.title: Sign in
access.login.wrong: Email address or password is not correct.
access.login.wrongDetail: Check what you entered. After several failed attempts you have to wait a while.
access.login.expiredDetail: Sign in again to continue where you left off.
access.login.noAccount: No account yet? Ask an admin of your organization for an invitation.
access.setup.title: Set up {product}
access.setup.code.title: Confirm this server
access.setup.code.lead: {product} is new on this server. The setup code shows that you have access to the server.
access.setup.code.label: Setup code
access.setup.code.hint: Case, spaces and dashes do not matter.
access.setup.code.restartNote: After a restart of the server a new code applies.
access.setup.code.wrong: The code is not correct. Copy it again from “setup-token.txt”; after several failed attempts you have to wait a while.
access.setup.code.wrongFixed: The code is not correct. Use the value of KALZIT_SETUP_TOKEN; after several failed attempts you have to wait a while.
access.setup.code.rateLimited: Too many failed attempts from this device. Wait a moment; the button counts down the time.
access.setup.code.ok: Code confirmed. It stays valid until setup is complete.
access.setup.where.title: Where do I find the code?
access.setup.where.fileText: On its first start the server puts the code into its data directory. Only someone with access to the server can read the file.
access.setup.where.fileDefaults: These are the default paths; with a data directory of your own the file is there.
access.setup.where.logText: At start the log says where the code is; it never contains the code itself.
access.setup.where.logHint: Linux with systemd: {command}. Otherwise the output of the process or the container.
access.setup.where.dockerText: The image has no shell; Kalzit prints the code itself.
access.setup.where.fixedText: For automated installs the value of {variable} applies (at least 16 letters or digits). Then the server writes no file.
access.setup.already.title: {product} is already set up
access.setup.already.text: This server already has an owner account and the setup code is deleted. Sign in with your account or ask an admin for an invitation.
access.setup.account.title: Your account
access.setup.account.lead: You sign in with it from now on. You invite more people later.
access.setup.account.name: Your name
access.setup.account.nameHint: This is how others see you in {product}.
access.setup.account.ownerNote: Your account becomes the owner of the first organization and a server admin.
access.setup.org.title: Your organization
access.setup.org.lead: The first organization on this server; your account becomes its owner.
access.setup.org.name: Organization name
access.setup.org.nameHint: Shown in the sidebar. You can add more organizations later.
access.setup.org.defaultsHint: They apply to everyone who has not chosen otherwise; each person can change them.
access.setup.org.timeZoneHint: For ranges like “today” in dashboards and for scheduled tasks.
access.setup.org.taken: Someone else has set up {product} in the meantime.
access.setup.org.takenDetail: What you entered was not saved. Sign in with the account created then, or ask for an invitation.
access.setup.org.codeChanged: The server was restarted; the setup code has changed.
access.setup.org.codeChangedDetail: Enter the new code. Name, email, password and organization stay filled in.
access.setup.done.title: All set, {name}.
access.setup.done.lead: {org} is set up and you are signed in.
access.setup.done.sourceText: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Prometheus, MongoDB, Elasticsearch and more. Each stays read-only.
access.setup.done.sampleText: A small SQLite database with orders, products and regions, read-only, to try things out.
access.setup.done.inviteText: Under Members, with roles and teams, whenever it suits you.
access.setup.done.codeDeleted: The setup code is deleted; the setup page is closed from now on.
access.help.title: Help
access.help.english: The guide is written in English.
access.invite.title: Welcome to {product}
access.invite.lead: Choose your name and a password.
access.invite.leadJoin: Accept the invitation to reach the dashboards and data of your organization.
access.invite.name: Your name
access.invite.expiredText: Invitations last seven days. Ask {name} or another admin for a new one.
access.invite.expiredTextAdmin: Invitations last seven days. Ask an admin of your organization for a new one.
access.invite.usedText: Each link works once. Sign in with your account.
access.invite.invalidText: The invitation was withdrawn or the link is incomplete. Check the link from the mail or ask for a new invitation.
access.invite.otherAccountText: The invitation is for {email}. Sign out to accept it.
access.invite.otherAccountShort: You are signed in with another account.
access.invite.accountExistsTitle: You already have an account on this server.
access.invite.accountExistsText: Sign in; then you are also a member of {org}, role {role}.
access.links.rateLimited: Too many links that do not work. Wait a few minutes.
access.reset.title: Reset password
access.reset.lead: We send you a link that works for 60 minutes.
access.reset.sentText: If there is an account with a password for {email}, a mail is on its way. The link works for 60 minutes.
access.reset.sentRetryIn: Nothing arrived? Check the spam folder. Next try in {time}.
access.reset.sentRetry: Nothing arrived? Check the spam folder and the address.
access.reset.rateLimited: Too many requests. Next try in {time}.
access.reset.noMailTitle: An admin of your organization can reset your password.
access.reset.noMailText: This server does not send mail.
access.reset.signOutEverywhere: Sign out on all other devices
access.reset.doneText: Other sessions have ended. Your second factor stays as it is.
access.reset.doneTextKept: Your other sessions go on. Your second factor stays as it is.
access.reset.invalidText: Password links work for 60 minutes and once. Just request a new one.
